open_points.subject: A01 create replay after erasure
open_points.text: “A create repeated after a lost answer … never silently makes a second project, customer or room” (R0-36), but A01 rule 8 says: “A request id leaves its record with the values anonymisation or erasure removes …; a create arriving after that with the same request id is a new create.”
open_points.question: After a Project is anonymised/deleted or a Customer is erased, must the former request id still identify a retry, or may that retry create a second record?
options: Keep a separate request-id tombstone so the retry cannot create another record
Allow reuse after erasure and explicitly narrow the replay guarantee
Retain the request id in the erased/anonymised record
open_points.default_guess: Keep a non-personal request-id tombstone and refuse or replay the later create.

open_points.subject: A13 expired confirmation handling
open_points.text: “an expired one is refused and cleared by any submission that reaches the confirmation check, whatever value it gives” conflicts with “A submission … giving another value, is refused and leaves the pending value as it was.”
open_points.question: If the pending confirmation has expired and a submission supplies a different value, is the expired pending confirmation cleared or retained?
options: Clear every expired pending confirmation once the confirmation check is reached
Retain it when the supplied value differs and clear it only when matched
Clear expired confirmations before comparing the supplied value
open_points.default_guess: Clear it before comparing the supplied value.

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation binding digest
open_points.text: “kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order” does not define the encoding, field order, type representation, domain separation or digest algorithm.
open_points.question: How are an action, target, version and inputs converted into the confirmation-binding digest so every implementation compares the same values?
options: Define a canonical length-prefixed encoding and a named cryptographic digest
Use canonical JSON with specified field ordering and normalization
Store and compare the structured bound values instead of a digest
open_points.default_guess: Use a domain-separated, length-prefixed canonical encoding hashed with SHA-256.

open_points.subject: A13 owner-session cookie scope
open_points.text: The session is “carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin.” Cookie scope is not defined by origin and the required Domain, Path, SameSite and local-HTTP behaviour are unstated.
open_points.question: What exact cookie attributes and host/path rules enforce the intended scope, and may the cookie be sent to Registry's service-API routes on the same host?
options: Use a host-only `__Host-` cookie with Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and Path=/, and ignore it on service routes
Use separate explicit cookie policies for local HTTP and remote HTTPS access
Require HTTPS everywhere and use one host-only secure cookie
open_points.default_guess: Require HTTPS and use a host-only `__Host-` cookie with Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and Path=/; service routes ignore it.

open_points.subject: A16 import file identity
open_points.text: “The mapping names the file by its digest” and “closure.file_digest = digest(f)” do not say which digest is used or whether it covers the uploaded bytes or a parsed/canonical representation.
open_points.question: What exact value identifies an import file for confirmation, the migration closure and the audit entry?
options: Hash the exact uploaded bytes with a named cryptographic algorithm
Hash a canonical serialization of the parsed import
Record both a raw-file digest and a canonical-content digest
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 of the exact uploaded bytes, with the algorithm identified alongside the digest.

open_points.subject: A16 post-import backup in owner-only mode
open_points.text: A16 rule 10 says “right after it Registry makes a backup run,” while A18 rule 10 says an import repeated during an owner-only start has a backup run “at the next start with the tokens”; A18 rule 1 also says “an owner-only start makes no run.”
open_points.question: When an import is accepted during an owner-only start, is its backup attempted immediately or deferred until the next token-enabled start?
options: Defer it until the next token-enabled start
Permit the special post-import backup even in owner-only mode
Refuse imports in owner-only mode
open_points.default_guess: Defer the backup until the next token-enabled start, following A18's specific restore rule.

open_points.subject: A18 scheduled backup versus import backup
open_points.text: Registry “backs up its store once a day at 03:00 UTC,” but a missed run is made at start only “if no backup was made that UTC day”; the post-import run is extra and “besides it, at most one backup is made per UTC day.”
open_points.question: Does a checked post-import backup made earlier that UTC day satisfy or suppress that day's scheduled daily backup?
options: The post-import backup is extra and never suppresses the scheduled daily backup
Any checked backup that day satisfies the daily requirement
It suppresses only a missed-start catch-up, not a 03:00 run while Registry is running
open_points.default_guess: Treat the import backup as extra; still make the scheduled daily backup once.

open_points.subject: A18 backup encryption format
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” does not declare an encryption/authentication algorithm, nonce generation, authenticated metadata, file format or key-digest algorithm.
open_points.question: What cryptographic format must every release use so backups are confidential, tamper-detecting and restorable across releases?
options: Specify an authenticated-encryption envelope, nonce rules, authenticated metadata and algorithms
Delegate the complete format to the store engine and pin that engine's backup format
Leave the format release-specific and require each release to declare it
open_points.default_guess: Specify a versioned AES-256-GCM envelope with a fresh random nonce, authenticated metadata and SHA-256 key identifiers.

open_points.subject: A18 backup status-file recovery
open_points.text: “Each run writes its outcome and instant to a status file … which a restart keeps,” but no rule covers a missing, truncated, malformed or inconsistent status file.
open_points.question: What does Registry do at start when kept backups exist but the status file cannot be read or disagrees with them?
options: Reconstruct backup facts from kept backups and show the last outcome as unknown
Fail startup
Discard the status and report no backup until the next run
open_points.default_guess: Reconstruct the newest checked-backup facts from backup metadata, report the prior outcome as unknown and continue serving.

open_points.subject: Restoring an end-of-relationship mark
open_points.text: R0-89 says the governance record names each repeated action “by its date, kind and the `customer_ref` or `project_id` it touched,” but ending a relationship has both an action instant and an owner-supplied effective end date, which may be earlier.
open_points.question: Which date does the recovery record preserve for an ended relationship, and how is the original effective end date recovered?
options: The recorded date is the effective relationship-end date
Record both the action instant and the effective end date
Use the restoration date as the new effective end date
open_points.default_guess: Record and replay the original effective relationship-end date separately from the action instant.

open_points.subject: Replaying an erased project after restore
open_points.text: R0-89 lists “erasures, restrictions, ends of a relationship” for repetition, and A18 says to bring each project to the recorded erased state, but erasing a project is refused while it is active and the recovery record does not say that a post-backup archive action is retained or replayed.
open_points.question: If the backup contains an active project that was later archived and erased, how may the owner reproduce the erasure after restore?
options: The governance record must also retain and replay the archive action before the erasure
Recovery may archive the project at restoration time and then erase it
Add a recovery-only operation that can erase the active restored record
open_points.default_guess: Require the governance record to include the archive action and replay it before the erasure.
